sources_found.name: DEQ Wildfire Smoke Trends and the AQI (May 2023 report)
sources_found.what: Official per-city inventory of wildfire-smoke AQI days. Portland: zero unhealthy-or-worse days 1985-2014; 2015-2022 = 26 days >=USG; the ONLY very-unhealthy (3) and hazardous (5) days all occurred in 2020; 2022 had three >=USG days from the Nakia Creek Fire, which made 'smokey conditions for around a week' in the Portland metro (Oct 2022).

sources_found.name: DEQ Wildfire Smoke Trends report, data 2000-2025
sources_found.what: Updated inventory: Portland 2013-2025 = 29 days >=USG; largest impacts 2017 (8 d), 2018 (6 d), 2020 (9 d incl. all very-unhealthy/hazardous days); zero >=USG days in 2025. Derived arithmetic from the two DEQ reports: 2021 had zero >=USG days and 2023+2024 combined had at most 1 — i.e., NO post-2020 Portland episode approaches Sept 2020 severity.

sources_found.name: JOHS daily smoke-shelter news releases, Sept 2020 (e.g., Sept 18 'ninth day' release)
sources_found.what: Day-by-day operational record of the two cleaner-air shelters: Oregon Convention Center from Sept 10, Charles Jordan CC from Sept 11, Mt. Scott CC on standby; 9 consecutive days ending ~Sept 18-19; context of ~1,400 year-round beds; 211info alert signup (text 'pdxshelter' to 898211). CRITICAL ABSENCE: none of the releases (Sept 14 and Sept 18 fetched in full) report occupancy or guest counts.
sources_found.access: open web pages; one release per day Sept 12-18 confirmed to exist

sources_found.name: Multnomah County January 2024 Severe Winter Weather After Action Report
sources_found.what: 44-page county AAR containing 'Figure 1: Daily Peak Numbers by facility' with per-facility nightly Guests/Capacity (nightly totals 276, 761, 1,076, 1,253, 1,292, 1,356), plus staffing, transports, health-impact counts. PROVES the county tabulates per-facility nightly occupancy for emergency shelter activations — exactly the record type a public-records request for Sept 2020 would target.

sources_found.name: Multnomah County severe-weather shelter usage news releases (winter events)
sources_found.what: Fetched Feb 15, 2024 release: 'About 200 people stayed in the 480 additional severe weather beds ... last night'; names 5 shelters; 211info coordinated 51 rides. Search results show the same nightly-count practice for Feb 2025 (684 people in seasonal+severe-weather spaces) and winter 2021-22 (2,377 bed nights over an 11-day cold event). These are aggregate nightly totals, published only for COLD events — no equivalent releases exist for smoke events.

sources_found.name: Multnomah County Public Records Requests (Oregon Public Records Law route)
sources_found.what: County page: requests governed by 'ORS 192.311 to 192.431'; submitted via the online Public Records Request Portal (manage request, pay invoices, download records); fees for staff research with advance notice; fee waiver/reduction 'if your request is in the public interest.' Route (describe only, not filed): request to the Homeless Services Department (JOHS successor) for nightly guest counts / shelter logs for the Sept 10-19, 2020 cleaner-air shelter activation — the Jan 2024 AAR shows this record type is compiled.
sources_found.coverage: all county departments incl. Homeless Services

sources_found.name: HSD Emergency Shelter Report page + HSD Data Dashboard
sources_found.what: Emergency Shelter Report (Mar 31, 2025) is a best-practices review, no occupancy data. The HSD Data Dashboard is a MONTHLY Tableau tool (people experiencing homelessness; served with housing/shelter/prevention) — system-level, not per-facility or nightly, and no severe-weather/smoke module visible on the page.

sources_found.name: Stories from the Outside: Oregon Wildfires 2020 (PSU HRAC)
sources_found.what: The n=73 survey already used by the study — page confirmed live (HTTP 200). Search-level detail: surveyed June 2021 with Street Roots Ambassadors; 75% received no information about support during the wildfire event; 69% received no help; 15% went to hospital.

sources_found.name: The Pathways Study (PSU HRAC for Multnomah County HSD, published Apr 9, 2026)
sources_found.what: NEW post-2020 survey of 541 people experiencing homelessness in Multnomah County (~10 months of surveying) on how they perceive, access, and navigate services incl. shelter; guided by lived-experience committee (TREES); funded by HSD. PDF exists (HTTP 200, 4.5 MB — content not read). Candidate updated source for awareness/shelter-choice parameters; smoke-specific content UNKNOWN.

sources_found.name: 211info
sources_found.what: 211 was the official signup channel for shelter alerts in Sept 2020 (per fetched JOHS release) and coordinates severe-weather shelter transportation (51 rides Feb 2024, 112 rides Feb 2025 per county releases). Search-level: 2024 volume 522,877 requests incl. 255,505 calls; a Data Team produces reports for stakeholders; quarterly reports page exists but returned 403 to automated fetch. NO open contact-volume dataset found; category/date-level contact data would require asking 211info's data team (do not contact — route only). NOTE: the data.oregon.gov 'Volume of Requests' dataset (ppyw-yvxy) is DEQ records-request stats, NOT 211info — verified by fetching its API metadata.
sources_found.coverage: Oregon + SW Washington; volumes cited for 2024
sources_found.access: reports pages open; raw contact data = data request to 211info

sources_found.name: EPA AirData pre-generated AQS files (monitor census + daily PM2.5)
sources_found.what: Downloaded and parsed annual_conc_by_monitor_2020: Multnomah County had exactly TWO PM2.5 sites reporting to AQS in 2020 — 41-051-0080 Portland SE Lafayette (FRM 88101 + 88502) and 41-051-2011 Portland Helensview School (88502 only). daily_88101_2020.zip also confirmed available (HTTP 200). Consequence: the regulatory network alone gives essentially no intra-county spatial resolution for Sept 2020.
sources_found.coverage: US, annual + daily files, 1980s-present; 2020 file verified

sources_found.name: Childs et al. daily wildfire smoke PM2.5 (Stanford ECHO Lab)
sources_found.what: THE spatially-resolved smoke-PM2.5 product covering Sept 2020: v1.0 (ES&T 2022) daily smoke PM2.5 for 2006-2020 at 10 km grid AND county, census-tract, and ZIP level (2 GB tract file); v2.0 beta extends 2006-2023. Open via Dropbox/Harvard Dataverse, replication code on GitHub.

sources_found.name: MAIAC MCD19A2 v6.1 AOD
sources_found.what: Daily 1-km Terra+Aqua MAIAC aerosol optical depth (incl. smoke injection height and AOD QA layers); distributed via LAADS DAAC and Google Earth Engine; product line covers Sept 2020. Caveat: AOD is not surface PM2.5, and retrieval completeness under the extremely dense Sept 2020 plume was not verified.

sources_found.name: EPA EQUATES (CMAQ modeled air quality)
sources_found.what: 12-km CONUS CMAQ daily surfaces — but spans 2002-2019 ONLY, so it does NOT cover Sept 2020. ABSENT for the study event. (Access when relevant: CMAS Data Warehouse, AWS Open Data, EPA RSIG.)

sources_found.name: Portland smoke episodes after the study event — news layer
sources_found.what: Oct 2022: DEQ advisory extended through the weekend; county's 3rd red-day wood-burning restriction that month (Oct 14, 2022). sources_found.name: IJGIS aims and scope
sources_found.what: Publisher page returned 403; text obtained from a third-party reproduction (myhuiban.com/journal/129) matching the T&F search capture: 'The aim of International Journal of Geographical Information Science is to provide a forum for the exchange of original ideas, approaches, methods and experiences in the field of GIScience.' Coverage bullets: 'Innovations and novel applications of GIScience in natural resources, social systems and the built environment'; 'Fundamental and computational issues of geographic information'; 'The design, implementation and use of geographical information for monitoring, prediction and decision making'; 'Novel geospatial approaches to address one or more of the UN SDGs.' Implication: an application must carry a methodological/GIScience contribution ('original ideas, approaches, methods'), not only a case study.
sources_found.access: open (via reproduction; publisher page blocks bots)

sources_found.name: Environmental Research Letters scope and publication criteria (IOP Publishing Support)
sources_found.what: Verbatim: ERL is 'the meeting place of research and policy communities concerned with the impact and outcomes of environmental change'; 'We expect the significance and impact of findings to be clearly communicated, demonstrating why the work is timely, requires urgent attention by a global audience, and demands rapid publication.' Decisive for this study — ERL will NOT accept: 'Local case studies (city-scale and smaller) which do not adequately show how results/findings are timely and significant in a broader context outside of the study area.' Letters max ~4,000 words; also discourages 'highly specialized or technical methodological research which is not accessible to a broad, multidisciplinary audience' (search capture of same support pages).

Any post-2020 Portland smoke episode of comparable severity to Sept 2020: DOES NOT EXIST through 2025 per DEQ's own trend reports — all very-unhealthy/hazardous Portland days on record occurred in 2020; Oct 2022 (3 days >=USG) and the ongoing Aug 2026 event (~AQI 160, unhealthy) are the only multi-day candidates, both in a far milder regime, and no dedicated Multnomah cleaner-air shelter activation was found for either — so a second Portland validation period lacks BOTH severity-matched exposure and shelter-use observations unless the Aug 2026 county response produces records.
Denver as a second city: no dedicated smoke-shelter or homeless smoke-response records found for 2020-2021 — weak candidate.
IJGIS aims-and-scope direct from Taylor & Francis: page returns 403 to automated fetch (text recovered via search capture + third-party reproduction).
PurpleAir sensor count/coverage in Portland during Sept 2020: not established (requires a PurpleAir API query).

An ongoing open dashboard of per-facility nightly severe-weather shelter occupancy in Multnomah County: none — the HSD Tableau dashboard is monthly and system-level; nightly counts appear only in news releases (totals) and after-action reports (per-facility).
Di et al. / other ~1-km ML PM2.5 surfaces covering Sept 2020: not verified in this pass (Childs et al. 10-km/tract product is the verified spatial smoke-PM2.5 coverage of the event).

Multnomah severe-weather/cleaner-air records specifically tied to smoke AFTER 2020: no smoke-shelter activation records found for 2021-2026; county guidance routes people to libraries/community centers as cleaner-air spaces.
notes: Method: WebSearch + WebFetch only; PDFs that WebFetch could not parse were downloaded and text-extracted locally with pypdf (files kept in the session scratchpad: deq_smoke_trends.txt, deq_smoke_trends_2025.txt, jan2024_aar.txt); no repo files were touched, no person or agency contacted, no forms submitted. Labeling: FETCHED = content opened/parsed or existence verified by direct HTTP request (HEAD-only cases are flagged in the entry); SEARCH-RESULT-ONLY = asserted by search captures I did not open. Key syntheses for the caller: (1) Independent Sept 2020 shelter-use observations exist only as unreleased county records — the records-request route is concrete and well-precedented (ORS 192.311-192.431, county portal, public-interest fee waiver; Jan 2024 AAR shows per-facility nightly Guests/Capacity is a record type the county produces). (2) Temporal out-of-sample validation inside Portland is severity-limited: DEQ's own record shows no post-2020 episode above 'unhealthy'; the honest framing is a milder-regime transfer test (Oct 2022) or a prospective test on the live Aug 2026 episode, whose operational records will be requestable soon. (3) Spatially-resolved PM2.5 for Sept 2020: 2 AQS sites county-wide (verified from EPA's file) make the regulatory network insufficient; the workable stack is PurpleAir (paid API), Childs et al. daily 10-km/tract smoke PM2.5 (open, covers event), NOAA HMS polygons (open), MAIAC 1-km AOD (open, caveats); EQUATES ends 2019 and is out. (4) Candidate facilities: RLIS footprints+heights (ODbL) + PP&R center list assemble an inventory; floor area partial, HVAC data absent. (5) Second city: Seattle/King County dominates (same Sept 2020 event, a dedicated healthy-air center with a reported ~80 served, HMIS/data-hub infrastructure, 2022 Bolt Creek repeat episode); Spokane moderate; Sacramento weak for 2018 but building clean-air shelters now; Denver effectively absent. (6) Journal fit: IJGIS requires a GIScience methods contribution ('original ideas, approaches, methods'); ERL explicitly rejects city-scale case studies that do not show significance 'in a broader context outside of the study area' — the quoted sentences are in the two journal entries. Caution on one derived number: 'at most 1 >=USG Portland day across 2023-2024' is arithmetic across the two DEQ reports' totals (26 days 2015-2022; 29 days 2013-2025 with 2 before 2015-era recount and 0 in 2025), not a sentence either report states.
